chapter_title: Ethers and Epoxides; Thiols and Sulfides

questions.chapter_title: Ethers and Epoxides; Thiols and Sulfides
questions.question: What is the mechanistic limitation of the Williamson ether synthesis when using a tertiary alkyl halide?

options.label: A
options.text: The strongly basic alkoxide performs rapid E2 elimination on the tertiary alkyl halide rather than SN2 substitution, yielding an alkene.

options.label: B
options.text: The alkoxide decomposes into carbon monoxide.

options.label: C
options.text: The reaction proceeds with retention of configuration.

options.label: D
options.text: The tertiary halide undergoes rapid homolytic polymerization.

questions.correct_answer: The strongly basic alkoxide performs rapid E2 elimination on the tertiary alkyl halide rather than SN2 substitution, yielding an alkene.
questions.explanation: Tertiary alkyl halides are too sterically hindered for SN2 backside attack; basic alkoxides exclusively undergo E2 elimination.

questions.chapter_title: Ethers and Epoxides; Thiols and Sulfides
questions.topic: Acidic Cleavage of Dialkyl Ethers Mechanism
questions.question: In the cleavage of diethyl ether by excess concentrated HI, what are the sequential mechanistic steps?

options.label: A
options.text: Homolytic cleavage into ethyl radicals followed by iodination.

options.label: B
options.text: E1 elimination to ethylene followed by HI addition.

options.label: C
options.text: Protonation of ether oxygen to an oxonium ion → SN2 displacement by iodide to yield ethyl iodide and ethanol → protonation of ethanol → second SN2 displacement to yield a second ethyl iodide.

options.label: D
options.text: Direct insertion of iodine into C-O bonds.

questions.correct_answer: Protonation of ether oxygen to an oxonium ion → SN2 displacement by iodide to yield ethyl iodide and ethanol → protonation of ethanol → second SN2 displacement to yield a second ethyl iodide.
questions.explanation: Strongly acidic HI protonates the ether oxygen into a good leaving group, enabling sequential SN2 displacements by nucleophilic iodide.

questions.chapter_title: Ethers and Epoxides; Thiols and Sulfides
questions.question: What is the structure of the 'butterfly' transition state during mCPBA epoxidation of an alkene?

options.label: A
options.text: A stepwise carbocation intermediate captured by carboxylate.

options.label: B
options.text: A free oxygen radical intermediate.

options.label: C
options.text: A concerted, single-step transition state where the peroxy oxygen is transferred to the π bond simultaneously with proton transfer to the peroxy carbonyl.

options.label: D
options.text: A 4-membered cyclic dioxetane ring.

questions.correct_answer: A concerted, single-step transition state where the peroxy oxygen is transferred to the π bond simultaneously with proton transfer to the peroxy carbonyl.
questions.explanation: The peroxy acid epoxidation is a concerted syn-addition proceeding through a highly organized 'butterfly' transition state.

questions.chapter_title: Ethers and Epoxides; Thiols and Sulfides
questions.question: Why does acid-catalyzed methanolysis of 1,2-epoxypropane yield 2-methoxy-1-propanol as the major product?

options.label: A
options.text: The reaction proceeds via an SN2 attack at the less hindered carbon.

options.label: B
options.text: Methanol is a bulky base that attacks terminal positions.

options.label: C
options.text: Protonation of the epoxide creates substantial partial carbocation character at the more substituted C2 carbon, directing the weak methanol nucleophile there.

options.label: D
options.text: The epoxide undergoes a 1,2-hydride shift before attack.

questions.correct_answer: Protonation of the epoxide creates substantial partial carbocation character at the more substituted C2 carbon, directing the weak methanol nucleophile there.
questions.explanation: Under acidic conditions, electronic factors dominate: the protonated epoxide has a longer, weaker bond to the more substituted carbon (greater positive charge).

questions.chapter_title: Ethers and Epoxides; Thiols and Sulfides
questions.question: Why does basic methanolysis (NaOCH₃ / CH₃OH) of 1,2-epoxypropane yield 1-methoxy-2-propanol exclusively?

options.label: A
options.text: C2 is deactivated by hyperconjugation.

options.label: B
options.text: Methoxide coordinates to oxygen prior to elimination.

options.label: C
options.text: The basic epoxide forms a free carbocation at C1.

options.label: D
options.text: Under basic conditions, the strong methoxide nucleophile attacks the less sterically hindered carbon (C1) in a classic SN2 pathway with inversion.

questions.correct_answer: Under basic conditions, the strong methoxide nucleophile attacks the less sterically hindered carbon (C1) in a classic SN2 pathway with inversion.
questions.explanation: Basic nucleophiles attack unprotonated epoxides via pure SN2 kinetics, governed entirely by steric accessibility at the less substituted carbon.

questions.chapter_title: Ethers and Epoxides; Thiols and Sulfides
questions.question: How does 18-crown-6 mechanistically enhance the nucleophilicity of potassium cyanide in benzene?

options.label: A
options.text: 18-crown-6 forms covalent bonds with benzene solvent.

options.label: B
options.text: 18-crown-6 coordinates K⁺ into its central cavity via ion-dipole interactions with 6 ethereal oxygens, leaving CN⁻ 'naked', unsolvated, and hyper-reactive.

options.label: C
options.text: 18-crown-6 donates protons to cyanide.

options.label: D
options.text: 18-crown-6 oxidizes potassium metal.

questions.correct_answer: 18-crown-6 coordinates K⁺ into its central cavity via ion-dipole interactions with 6 ethereal oxygens, leaving CN⁻ 'naked', unsolvated, and hyper-reactive.
questions.explanation: Encapsulation of the cation in nonpolar solvents produces 'naked' anions with enormous nucleophilic reactivity.

questions.chapter_title: Ethers and Epoxides; Thiols and Sulfides
questions.question: What is the mechanistic pathway for the oxidation of two thiols to a disulfide by molecular iodine (I₂)?

options.label: A
options.text: Direct reduction of iodine to iodate.

options.label: B
options.text: Homolytic cleavage of sulfur-carbon bonds.

options.label: C
options.text: Nucleophilic attack of thiol sulfur on I₂ yields a sulfenyl iodide intermediate (R-SI), which is attacked by a second thiol with displacement of iodide.

options.label: D
options.text: Formation of a sulfur trioxide adduct.

questions.correct_answer: Nucleophilic attack of thiol sulfur on I₂ yields a sulfenyl iodide intermediate (R-SI), which is attacked by a second thiol with displacement of iodide.
questions.explanation: The reaction proceeds via a sulfenyl iodide intermediate that is rapidly displaced by a second thiolate nucleophile to forge the S-S bridge.

questions.chapter_title: Ethers and Epoxides; Thiols and Sulfides
questions.question: Why is dithiothreitol (DTT / Cleland's reagent) exceptionally effective at reducing protein disulfide bridges?

options.label: A
options.text: DTT undergoes sequential thiol-disulfide exchange, forming a thermodynamically stable six-membered cyclic disulfide ring that drives the reduction to completion.

options.label: B
options.text: DTT precipitates proteins from solution.

options.label: C
options.text: DTT is a strong Brønsted acid that hydrolyzes disulfides.

options.label: D
options.text: DTT releases gaseous hydrogen that hydrogenates the disulfide.

questions.correct_answer: DTT undergoes sequential thiol-disulfide exchange, forming a thermodynamically stable six-membered cyclic disulfide ring that drives the reduction to completion.
questions.explanation: Formation of an entropically and enthalpically favored six-membered ring drives quantitative reduction of intermolecular disulfides.

questions.chapter_title: Ethers and Epoxides; Thiols and Sulfides
questions.question: Why do dialkyl sulfides react with alkyl halides much faster than dialkyl ethers via SN2?

options.label: A
options.text: Sulfur has larger, more polarizable 3p nonbonding lone pairs that attack electrophilic carbons with lower activation energy than compact 2p oxygen lone pairs.

options.label: B
options.text: Sulfur forms ionic bonds with carbon.

options.label: C
options.text: Sulfides are strong Brønsted acids.

options.label: D
options.text: Sulfur is more electronegative than oxygen.

questions.correct_answer: Sulfur has larger, more polarizable 3p nonbonding lone pairs that attack electrophilic carbons with lower activation energy than compact 2p oxygen lone pairs.
questions.explanation: Greater polarizability makes sulfur a far superior nucleophile compared to oxygen in SN2 displacements.

questions.chapter_title: Ethers and Epoxides; Thiols and Sulfides
questions.question: In the Sharpless epoxidation of allylic alcohols, what components assemble the chiral catalyst?

options.label: A
options.text: Rhodium chloride and chiral phosphines.

options.label: B
options.text: Palladium acetate and BINAP.

options.label: C
options.text: Titanium(IV) isopropoxide [Ti(OiPr)₄], chiral diethyl tartrate (DET), and tert-butyl hydroperoxide (TBHP) coordinate to deliver oxygen enantioselectively.

options.label: D
options.text: Osmium tetroxide, NMO, and chiral quinine.

questions.correct_answer: Titanium(IV) isopropoxide [Ti(OiPr)₄], chiral diethyl tartrate (DET), and tert-butyl hydroperoxide (TBHP) coordinate to deliver oxygen enantioselectively.
questions.explanation: The chiral titanium-tartrate dimer coordinates both the allylic alcohol and peroxide, transferring oxygen exclusively to one enantiotopic face.

options.text: Sulfur forms ionic bonds with carbon.

options.label: B
options.text: Sulfur is more electronegative than oxygen.

options.label: C
options.text: Sulfur has larger, more polarizable 3p nonbonding lone pairs that attack electrophilic carbons with lower activation energy than compact 2p oxygen lone pairs.

options.label: D
options.text: Sulfides are strong Brønsted acids.

questions.correct_answer: Sulfur has larger, more polarizable 3p nonbonding lone pairs that attack electrophilic carbons with lower activation energy than compact 2p oxygen lone pairs.
questions.explanation: Greater polarizability makes sulfur a far superior nucleophile compared to oxygen in SN2 displacements.

questions.chapter_title: Ethers and Epoxides; Thiols and Sulfides
questions.question: In the Sharpless epoxidation of allylic alcohols, what components assemble the chiral catalyst?

options.label: A
options.text: Osmium tetroxide, NMO, and chiral quinine.

options.label: B
options.text: Palladium acetate and BINAP.

options.label: C
options.text: Titanium(IV) isopropoxide [Ti(OiPr)₄], chiral diethyl tartrate (DET), and tert-butyl hydroperoxide (TBHP) coordinate to deliver oxygen enantioselectively.

options.label: D
options.text: Rhodium chloride and chiral phosphines.

questions.correct_answer: Titanium(IV) isopropoxide [Ti(OiPr)₄], chiral diethyl tartrate (DET), and tert-butyl hydroperoxide (TBHP) coordinate to deliver oxygen enantioselectively.
questions.explanation: The chiral titanium-tartrate dimer coordinates both the allylic alcohol and peroxide, transferring oxygen exclusively to one enantiotopic face.

questions.chapter_title: Ethers and Epoxides; Thiols and Sulfides
questions.question: What is the mechanistic limitation of the Williamson ether synthesis when using a tertiary alkyl halide?

options.label: A
options.text: The alkoxide decomposes into carbon monoxide.

options.label: B
options.text: The strongly basic alkoxide performs rapid E2 elimination on the tertiary alkyl halide rather than SN2 substitution, yielding an alkene.

options.label: C
options.text: The reaction proceeds with retention of configuration.

options.label: D
options.text: The tertiary halide undergoes rapid homolytic polymerization.

questions.correct_answer: The strongly basic alkoxide performs rapid E2 elimination on the tertiary alkyl halide rather than SN2 substitution, yielding an alkene.
questions.explanation: Tertiary alkyl halides are too sterically hindered for SN2 backside attack; basic alkoxides exclusively undergo E2 elimination.

questions.chapter_title: Ethers and Epoxides; Thiols and Sulfides
questions.topic: Acidic Cleavage of Dialkyl Ethers Mechanism
questions.question: In the cleavage of diethyl ether by excess concentrated HI, what are the sequential mechanistic steps?

options.label: A
options.text: Homolytic cleavage into ethyl radicals followed by iodination.

options.label: B
options.text: Protonation of ether oxygen to an oxonium ion → SN2 displacement by iodide to yield ethyl iodide and ethanol → protonation of ethanol → second SN2 displacement to yield a second ethyl iodide.

options.label: C
options.text: Direct insertion of iodine into C-O bonds.

options.label: D
options.text: E1 elimination to ethylene followed by HI addition.

questions.correct_answer: Protonation of ether oxygen to an oxonium ion → SN2 displacement by iodide to yield ethyl iodide and ethanol → protonation of ethanol → second SN2 displacement to yield a second ethyl iodide.
questions.explanation: Strongly acidic HI protonates the ether oxygen into a good leaving group, enabling sequential SN2 displacements by nucleophilic iodide.

questions.chapter_title: Ethers and Epoxides; Thiols and Sulfides
questions.question: What is the structure of the 'butterfly' transition state during mCPBA epoxidation of an alkene?

options.label: A
options.text: A stepwise carbocation intermediate captured by carboxylate.

options.label: B
options.text: A 4-membered cyclic dioxetane ring.

options.label: C
options.text: A concerted, single-step transition state where the peroxy oxygen is transferred to the π bond simultaneously with proton transfer to the peroxy carbonyl.

options.label: D
options.text: A free oxygen radical intermediate.

questions.correct_answer: A concerted, single-step transition state where the peroxy oxygen is transferred to the π bond simultaneously with proton transfer to the peroxy carbonyl.
questions.explanation: The peroxy acid epoxidation is a concerted syn-addition proceeding through a highly organized 'butterfly' transition state.

questions.chapter_title: Ethers and Epoxides; Thiols and Sulfides
questions.question: Why does acid-catalyzed methanolysis of 1,2-epoxypropane yield 2-methoxy-1-propanol as the major product?

options.label: A
options.text: Protonation of the epoxide creates substantial partial carbocation character at the more substituted C2 carbon, directing the weak methanol nucleophile there.

options.label: B
options.text: Methanol is a bulky base that attacks terminal positions.

options.label: C
options.text: The reaction proceeds via an SN2 attack at the less hindered carbon.

options.label: D
options.text: The epoxide undergoes a 1,2-hydride shift before attack.

questions.correct_answer: Protonation of the epoxide creates substantial partial carbocation character at the more substituted C2 carbon, directing the weak methanol nucleophile there.
questions.explanation: Under acidic conditions, electronic factors dominate: the protonated epoxide has a longer, weaker bond to the more substituted carbon (greater positive charge).

questions.chapter_title: Ethers and Epoxides; Thiols and Sulfides
questions.question: Why does basic methanolysis (NaOCH₃ / CH₃OH) of 1,2-epoxypropane yield 1-methoxy-2-propanol exclusively?

options.label: A
options.text: Methoxide coordinates to oxygen prior to elimination.

options.label: B
options.text: The basic epoxide forms a free carbocation at C1.

options.label: C
options.text: C2 is deactivated by hyperconjugation.

options.label: D
options.text: Under basic conditions, the strong methoxide nucleophile attacks the less sterically hindered carbon (C1) in a classic SN2 pathway with inversion.

questions.correct_answer: Under basic conditions, the strong methoxide nucleophile attacks the less sterically hindered carbon (C1) in a classic SN2 pathway with inversion.
questions.explanation: Basic nucleophiles attack unprotonated epoxides via pure SN2 kinetics, governed entirely by steric accessibility at the less substituted carbon.

questions.chapter_title: Ethers and Epoxides; Thiols and Sulfides
questions.question: How does 18-crown-6 mechanistically enhance the nucleophilicity of potassium cyanide in benzene?

options.label: A
options.text: 18-crown-6 donates protons to cyanide.

options.label: B
options.text: 18-crown-6 coordinates K⁺ into its central cavity via ion-dipole interactions with 6 ethereal oxygens, leaving CN⁻ 'naked', unsolvated, and hyper-reactive.

options.label: C
options.text: 18-crown-6 forms covalent bonds with benzene solvent.

options.label: D
options.text: 18-crown-6 oxidizes potassium metal.

questions.correct_answer: 18-crown-6 coordinates K⁺ into its central cavity via ion-dipole interactions with 6 ethereal oxygens, leaving CN⁻ 'naked', unsolvated, and hyper-reactive.
questions.explanation: Encapsulation of the cation in nonpolar solvents produces 'naked' anions with enormous nucleophilic reactivity.

questions.chapter_title: Ethers and Epoxides; Thiols and Sulfides
questions.question: What is the mechanistic pathway for the oxidation of two thiols to a disulfide by molecular iodine (I₂)?

options.label: A
options.text: Nucleophilic attack of thiol sulfur on I₂ yields a sulfenyl iodide intermediate (R-SI), which is attacked by a second thiol with displacement of iodide.

options.label: B
options.text: Direct reduction of iodine to iodate.

options.label: C
options.text: Homolytic cleavage of sulfur-carbon bonds.

options.label: D
options.text: Formation of a sulfur trioxide adduct.

questions.correct_answer: Nucleophilic attack of thiol sulfur on I₂ yields a sulfenyl iodide intermediate (R-SI), which is attacked by a second thiol with displacement of iodide.
questions.explanation: The reaction proceeds via a sulfenyl iodide intermediate that is rapidly displaced by a second thiolate nucleophile to forge the S-S bridge.

questions.chapter_title: Ethers and Epoxides; Thiols and Sulfides
questions.question: Why is dithiothreitol (DTT / Cleland's reagent) exceptionally effective at reducing protein disulfide bridges?

options.label: A
options.text: DTT precipitates proteins from solution.

options.label: B
options.text: DTT undergoes sequential thiol-disulfide exchange, forming a thermodynamically stable six-membered cyclic disulfide ring that drives the reduction to completion.

options.label: C
options.text: DTT is a strong Brønsted acid that hydrolyzes disulfides.

options.label: D
options.text: DTT releases gaseous hydrogen that hydrogenates the disulfide.

questions.correct_answer: DTT undergoes sequential thiol-disulfide exchange, forming a thermodynamically stable six-membered cyclic disulfide ring that drives the reduction to completion.
questions.explanation: Formation of an entropically and enthalpically favored six-membered ring drives quantitative reduction of intermolecular disulfides.
